instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
CTE returning count per caller_id
output: WITH counts AS (SELECT caller_id, COUNT(*) c FROM calls GROUP BY caller_id) SELECT * FROM counts WHERE c > 2;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
CTE computing average callee_id
output: WITH avg_cte AS (SELECT AVG(callee_id) a FROM calls) SELECT * FROM calls WHERE callee_id > (SELECT a FROM avg_cte);

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Two CTEs joined together
output: WITH a AS (SELECT caller_id, SUM(callee_id) s FROM calls GROUP BY caller_id), b AS (SELECT caller_id, COUNT(*) c FROM calls GROUP BY caller_id) SELECT a.caller_id, a.s FROM a JOIN b ON a.caller_id = b.caller_id WHERE b.c > 3;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Apply filters before entering a CTE
output: WITH filtered AS (SELECT * FROM calls WHERE callee_id > 50) SELECT caller_id, COUNT(*) FROM filtered GROUP BY caller_id;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
CTE then order by aggregate
output: WITH total AS (SELECT caller_id, SUM(callee_id) s FROM calls GROUP BY caller_id) SELECT * FROM total ORDER BY s DESC;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Modify via CTE then select window rank
output: WITH base AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY caller_id ORDER BY callee_id DESC) rn FROM calls) SELECT * FROM base WHERE rn = 1;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Recursive CTE to create a number sequence
output: WITH RECURSIVE num(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM num WHERE n < 10) SELECT * FROM num;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Recursive CTE walking a holiday-date chain
output: WITH RECURSIVE dates(d) AS (SELECT '2024-01-01'::date UNION ALL SELECT (d + INTERVAL '1 day')::date FROM dates WHERE d < '2024-01-10') SELECT d FROM dates;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
CTE combining two aggregates in one pass
output: WITH agg AS (SELECT caller_id, SUM(callee_id) s, AVG(callee_id) a FROM calls GROUP BY caller_id) SELECT caller_id, s, a FROM agg WHERE s > 100;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Multiple CTEs chained (a then b referencing a)
output: WITH a AS (SELECT caller_id, COUNT(*) c FROM calls GROUP BY caller_id), b AS (SELECT * FROM a WHERE c > 1) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM b;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Set expressions inside a CTE
output: WITH c AS (SELECT caller_id FROM calls WHERE callee_id > 10 UNION SELECT caller_id FROM calls WHERE callee_id < 2) SELECT * FROM c;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
CTE for deduplication using row number
output: WITH dedup AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY caller_id ORDER BY duration) rn FROM calls) SELECT * FROM dedup WHERE rn = 1;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Recursive hierarchy emulating parent-child with depth
output: WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (SELECT id, caller_id FROM calls WHERE parent_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT c.id, c.caller_id FROM calls c JOIN tree t ON c.parent_id = t.id) SELECT * FROM tree;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Materialize then refilter a CTE
output: WITH m AS (SELECT caller_id, SUM(callee_id) s FROM calls GROUP BY caller_id HAVING SUM(callee_id) > 0) SELECT *, s * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(s) FROM m) AS share FROM m;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Tally CTE feeding a LEFT JOIN to fill missing grouping rows
output: WITH RECURSIVE grp AS (SELECT 1 g UNION ALL SELECT g + 1 FROM grp WHERE g < 10) SELECT g, COUNT(t.caller_id) FROM grp LEFT JOIN calls t ON t.caller_id = g GROUP BY g;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
CTE with ordered window and outer filter on rank
output: WITH r AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY caller_id ORDER BY callee_id DESC) rk FROM calls) SELECT * FROM r WHERE rk <= 3;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
CTE used twice via self reference pattern
output: WITH c AS (SELECT caller_id, callee_id FROM calls WHERE callee_id IS NOT NULL) SELECT * FROM c WHERE callee_id > (SELECT AVG(callee_id) FROM c);

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Inline aggregate then filter in outer query
output: WITH g AS (SELECT caller_id FROM calls GROUP BY caller_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2) SELECT * FROM calls WHERE caller_id IN (SELECT * FROM g);

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Pivot-like pivot using multiple aggregate CTEs
output: WITH wide AS (SELECT caller_id, SUM(CASE WHEN callee_id > 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over100, SUM(CASE WHEN callee_id <= 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) under FROM calls GROUP BY caller_id) SELECT * FROM wide;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Recursive CTE to expand an interval of ranges
output: WITH RECURSIVE iv(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1 FROM iv WHERE n < 100) SELECT n FROM iv;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
CTE for lead-lag difference
output: WITH lg AS (SELECT caller_id, callee_id, LAG(callee_id) OVER (PARTITION BY caller_id ORDER BY duration) prev FROM calls) SELECT *, callee_id - COALESCE(prev,callee_id) AS delta FROM lg;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Chained CTEs for multi-stage business calc
output: WITH step1 AS (SELECT caller_id, SUM(callee_id) s FROM calls GROUP BY caller_id), step2 AS (SELECT *, s * 2 doubled FROM step1) SELECT * FROM step2 WHERE doubled > 20;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
CTE referencing a correlated subquery
output: WITH big AS (SELECT caller_id FROM calls GROUP BY caller_id HAVING SUM(callee_id) > 100) SELECT * FROM calls t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM big b WHERE b.caller_id = t.caller_id);

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
Recursive CTE producing factorial numbers
output: WITH RECURSIVE f(n, fact) AS (SELECT 1, 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1, fact*(n+1) FROM f WHERE n < 10) SELECT * FROM f;

instruction:
Schema: calls(caller_id, callee_id, duration)
CTE on itself to compute growth from prior period
output: WITH p AS (SELECT caller_id, SUM(callee_id) cur FROM calls GROUP BY caller_id), q AS (SELECT *, LAG(cur) OVER (ORDER BY caller_id) prev FROM p) SELECT *, cur - prev AS growth FROM q;
